items.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: And it could be Tommy and Frank Sinatra and the Nicholas Brothers or Charlie Barnet. And I’d sit there and say when am I going to do that?

ctx.x: Was your family surprised at the direction your career took?

No. Because they knew that’s what I wanted to do. That’s all I wanted to do. I never wanted to do anything else. I’m not proud of it. And people shouldn’t do what I’m saying, but I didn’t graduate high school because I spent all my time in the Paramount Theater when the new bands were coming. It was like empty in the school. I was one. I was the leader of empty. And it was an interesting thing because when we went to the Paramount Theater, we gave one guy 55 cents in the morning. And it was, you had Don Baker at…
and saw where I sat. I looked right there, and I went like this, I says thank you. I says I made it.
